text: In the real-life claims, if experience turns out better than expected, the savings will form part of the Fund and policyholders will benefit from it through premium rebates, slower premium growth or better payouts.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It will work hand in hand with personal and family savings, and Government and community support to help our future generations of Singaporeans afford long-term care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We know, however, that some among our existing cohorts may not join CareShield Life.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Others may need additional support beyond CareShield Life, and this is why we have decided to enhance our long-term care financing system in two other ways.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I agree with many Members that CareShield Life and the other two long-term care enhancements are not easy for Singaporeans to understand.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will initiate more communications and engagement efforts to explain the schemes to Singaporeans and how they can tap on them to support their long-term care needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I hope that, through this debate and our outreach efforts, Singaporeans will be more aware about their long-term care needs and start to think about their long-term care needs and to plan for them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I hope that we will all have good health and stay active and free from disability.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But should disability strike, we can have peace of mind that their long-term care needs are well supported.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, did you want to ask a clarification?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have a clarification for Mr Gan Kim Yong and also for Senior Minister of State Dr Amy Khor.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For Minister Gan, I think in his opening speech, he mentioned that the Government had set aside $2 billion for CareShield Life.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I wonder if he could elaborate on what this $2 billion is set aside for.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is it premium subsidies or does it also include the administrative cost of running the scheme or some other expenses?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: For Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, my clarifications relate to the decision to have gender-differentiated premiums for the scheme.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: She mentioned earlier that it was a difficult decision for MOH to make.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to clarify, first of all, that actually, there is no impediment to designing on a unisex basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In other words, it is a policy decision.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It could have been designed to have unisex premiums, but the Government has decided to take this gender-differentiated approach.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The second clarification is that Dr Amy Khor said earlier that MOH felt that to have gender differentiation was fairer on an actuarial basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But does Dr Amy Khor also not agree that this is actually a missed opportunity for policy to demonstrate important values, such as mutual support and solidarity?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And as Members can appreciate, the amount of funds that is needed also depends on the number of people from the existing cohorts that will be participating because some of the premium subsidies are allocated for the existing cohorts, and they have the option to either join the scheme or stay with ElderShield.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think that explains the basis of the $2 billion.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, as I have said, it is not an easy decision to make for the ESRC and, obviously, for us.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, when we made our decision, it must be on the principle that the scheme will be sustainable in the long term.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think that it is very important to ensure that the scheme is sustainable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the start of the scheme – when we implement it – CareShield Life is mandatory for future cohorts, but for existing cohorts, based on the various reasons that I have provided, the decision was that it will not be mandatory, but we would want to encourage as many as possible to come on the scheme.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if we do not determine the premiums on an actuarially correct basis, what it means is that there is likely to be some adverse selection.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the men actually pay less than women for the same age group and income level.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And if we equalise the CareShield Life premiums, they would know that they are paying more than what is actuarially determined.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, some may feel that they would not want to join the scheme and there would be dropouts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, private insurers may also offer lower premiums for men based on gender differentiation, and that would mean that more would opt out of the CareShield Life scheme and, at the end of the day, it could be unsustainable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I think what we want to do is to make sure that it is actuarially correctly determined.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note the issue about women having less savings, MediSave and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We think that it is prudent to determine the premiums correctly and then look at different ways to help the women.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, our means-tested premium subsidies actually already provide a higher quantum of subsidies for women because it is based on a percentage of premiums payable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, at the end of the day, anyone who is not able to pay for their premiums if they opt in to CareShield Life or they are in the mandatory cohort, the Government will assist with Additional Premium Support.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, no one would lose coverage because of financial difficulties.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition to that, of course, actually, for women, because they are more likely to become severely disabled as a result of longer lifespan, it means that, as I said earlier, those who claim are likely to claim for a longer period, too.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In MediShield Life, for instance, women actually pay premiums, on average, for a longer period because they have a longer lifespan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Of course, then they are covered over their longer lifespan.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the other point, sorry, what was it that the Member was asking me?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The first question was about whether the scheme could have been designed on a unisex basis.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: That means there is no impediment really; it is a policy decision.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And the second question is: while MOH justifies that as being fair actuarially, it has also missed the opportunity to show mutual support and solidarity.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we will continue to explore ways to look at how we can help women who face difficulties.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the missed opportunity, I do not think so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Besides having equal premiums, the fact is that family members, men, spouse or any loved ones, could already help the women with their premium payments by topping up their MediSave or using their MediSave to pay.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, in fact, it is a very good opportunity to promote strong family values and support through the scheme.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: May we request Members to keep their clarifications short ,and answers short as well?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: I think I have raised quite a number of questions and I do not really recall them being specifically answered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think Ms Chia Yong Yong asked about universality: why not we cover everybody?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think the Senior Ministers of State have replied.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think Ms Chia also asked why we were able to respond to the Committee in 24 hours.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we started already working on premium support and transitional subsidies and so on, and we hope to be able to give Singaporeans as complete a picture as possible when the report is out.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we have been working with them quite closely.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: By the time they released their report, it was no surprise to us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We already know and, in fact, most Singaporeans already know what the key recommendations are.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I think that is why we were able to accept the report quite quickly so that Singaporeans also would be able to know exactly what we have in mind in terms of premium support and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member also asked about how ElderShield premiums or Careshield Life premiums were determined – the methodology and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member also mentioned the specific suggestion whether we can integrate all the schemes to create synergy among all the schemes – ElderShield Scheme, CareShield Life, MediShield and CPF LIFE and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I agree that there are quite a lot of schemes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We must understand that each scheme has a specific purpose.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: CPF LIFE, for example, is targeted at retirement adequacy to ensure that you have sufficient support for daily living.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: MediShield Life is focused more on medical care which is very much service-centric, looking at the medical services, whereas ElderShield and CareShield Life are designed to be targeted at long-term care needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there are quite different objectives, different targets and different groups of policyholders as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And their risk profiles are also quite different.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we decided to keep them separate so that it is easier to understand each piece.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Of course, it will mean that it will take us a lot more effort to explain.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think it is better to spend the effort explaining to people on specific programmes, rather than to try to integrate them and create more confusion.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we do take the Member's point that there are many schemes, and it will need time for us to explain clearly and slowly, and we hope that Singaporeans will bear with us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It does take time for us to explain, to reach out to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even when we first launched MediShield Life, we took two to three years before we could really explain what MediShield Life is about.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If Members remember, we had a great problem explaining the Integrated Plan – how does MediShield Life interact with the Integrated Plans.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I hope Members will bear with us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I am taking a fair bit of time because you have quite a number of suggestions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I hope I have answered most of them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But should the Member have any specific one, she can raise it and I would be happy to answer.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: I know we often talk about the inability to perform the three ADLs, and that is always in the context of making a claim.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: But we have used severe disability in the context of excluding people from CareShield.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: I think we need to be very clear – are we talking about also three ADLs or something else?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: In relation to the eligibility for other assistance schemes, I also raised the point about whether we could streamline the application process.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Again, I know that Senior Minister of State Amy Khor mentioned about one single assessment but that is for claiming, not in relation to financial assistance across other schemes.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Also, the other point would be on the entity that will oversee, whether there will be overlays or gaps.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Again, I know Senior of State Chee Hong Tat mentioned that it would be administered by AIC in collaboration with CPF Board.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: So, I would like to know which entities would be having the overall oversight.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
text: Will it be MOH, the Ministry of Finance or is this going to be with MSF, a collaborative inter-Ministry oversight?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would try to be as fast as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Starting from the last question, with regard to the administration of the scheme, of course, MOH will be overall responsible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But AIC is the agency on the ground which is tending to the needs of the patients as well as those with long-term care needs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, they will be the frontline, whereas CPF Board will be administering the fund largely.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In terms of the application process, certainly, we will continue to see how we can streamline and make the claim process easier.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But when it comes to financial assistance, of course, we cannot do away with the need to do means-testing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the means-testing process will still have to be on the ground and our medical social workers and our MSF social workers will all be helping us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have also integrated the eldercare/senior care services on the ground by bringing SGO into AIC and we are expanding that community network for seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there are quite a lot of efforts on the ground to streamline the care support for the seniors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On severe disability, by and large, we refer to the three ADLs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And for the application to join CareShield Life, we encourage Singaporeans to join our CareShield Life as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So far, we try to include all of them – those who are not three ADLs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But please do not wait until you have two ADLs then you decide to join.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, I encourage you to join as soon as the scheme comes to you in 2021.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we want to make sure that we have a system that is stable and we can manage the scheme efficiently for this mandatory cohort because they will have to come onto the system in 2020.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And then, once that is done, then we will extend it to all the other Singaporeans from the existing cohorts, and the numbers are much larger.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Earlier, Dr Amy Khor shared, potentially, two million.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But of course, we do not think all two million will all join at the same time.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But two million people potentially could be applying to join the scheme.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why we want to stagger it to make sure that the administration of the scheme and the systems are done properly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Picking up from what she mentioned about loved ones topping up their spouses' MediSave, there is a point I raised in my speech about the prospect of the Government providing a tax relief like it does for Special Account, whether it could consider something similar for MediSave accounts, particularly in the gig economy, with contract work.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think that was a point Ms Jessica Tan raised as well.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Yes, I think for top-ups, there are already some tax incentives, but it is accrued to the recipients.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu
text: I think with all these moves in the ITLC financing sector, are there any considerations whether this might impact the MediSave contribution rate or the basic healthcare sum?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As I had shared in my earlier example in the speech, for the future cohorts of Singaporeans, the premiums that they have to pay using the MediSave for both schemes like CareShield Life as well as MediShield Life should be enough to pay for the premiums without them having to fork out cash.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But, of course, we know every situation is different.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There will be individuals who will need more help and that is why we have other support schemes that they can apply for, including Additional Premium Support.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Please direct your clarification to the specific Minister or —

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: This is on the point where the scheme allows members to withdraw cash from their MediSave account to support their long-term care needs.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: That means that a person must be certified to need long-term care, then only he/she can apply to withdraw cash from his/her MediSave?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: That means, anyone who needs long-term care can apply, and who will certify that the person needs long-term care?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And in addition to CareShield Life, if you have CareShield Life.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If not, MediSave – you can tap on it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is restricted to those who have three ADLs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The reason is because we want to ensure that there is sufficient balance in your MediSave.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And, therefore, the use of cash from MediSave has to be regulated by that criterion.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And assessment for eligibility in terms of severe disability is the same assessment as CareShield Life or ElderShield.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There was one more question about family members.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Part of the reason is also we want to minimise intergenerational transfer.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, between you and your spouse, we allow you to share your balances.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I just have three supplementary questions for Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I would just like to ask again if the Government will consider publishing the actuarial model in full, including details, such as the assumed medical loss ratio, the expected rate of payouts in the future, the capital adequacy ratio and so on, for the reason that such transparency may actually be more effective to get public buy-in and may actually interest more people to voluntarily come into the scheme if they are not mandated to do so because, from that disclosure, they will be able to see it is, in fact, a fair and a good scheme, presumably.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The second one is, I believe the position is that the independent Council will have the discretion to decide on premium rebates.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: For ElderShield, I think there are some guidance given to the three insurers about when they give up premium rebates, and how much.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, will the Government consider instituting some guidelines that will be binding on the independent Council to guide them on how to give out premium rebates, when and to what extent?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think this point was made by some other Members as well.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And the last one is really in terms of the way the funds will be managed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: If this is going to be managed by CPF Board, will the funds be managed in the same way as the CPF monies where I believe the Government of Singapore Investment Corporation plays some role in managing CPF monies through the instrument of Singapore Government securities?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And I think it is important to discuss with the experts because it is a technically very complicated complex scheme.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For example, I think loss ratio, for example, is not quite applicable for a scheme that is prefunded.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Loss ratios are actually more applicable to schemes like MediShield Life where it is year by year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, you can look at what the total amount of claims versus the premiums that you have collected – claims plus expenses – versus the amount of claims you have collected.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is more applicable for a scheme like MedisShield Life where you collect premiums in one year to provide coverage for that year.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But for prefunded schemes like ElderShield and CareShield Life, actually, loss ratio does not quite apply.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I just wanted to give this as an example to say that this is highly complex and, therefore, we will discuss with the Council and the actuaries on what is the best way to share the information in a meaningful manner.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: On the second question that Mr Perera raised about premium rebates, again, allow me to clarify.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is a difference between CareShield Life and the previous scheme, ElderShield, because ElderShield, first, is administered by private insurers and they are social entities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, embedded in their calculations, there will be a profit element.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And this safeguard, in a way, is to prevent them, if there are additional surpluses, that they will take the entire amount.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The second key difference is that the current ElderShield scheme, the payout is fixed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, there is no way to return something to policyholders, except through a rebate.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But for CareShield Life, because the payouts are designed to gradually increase over time, you can actually have more parameters that you can use to return some of these, if you have some additional balance amounts that you return it to policyholders, you want to benefit policyholders, there are ways to do it.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But certainly, the nature of the fund is such that you want to go for stable returns.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is an important consideration for long-term sustainability.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: We have spent half an hour on clarification.
